name: Zsolt Felcsuti
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Zsolt Felcsuti owns MPF Industry, a Swiss conglomerate that operates across central Europe.
He started the business in 1994 with his father, Csaba, a machinery parts company. They began acquiring other businesses in 2003.
Csaba Felcsuti operated his first business during the Communist era, which until 1989 limited the size of all private enterprise in the country.
MPF now sells products in about 30 countries.

name: Horst Wortmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Horst Wortmann, Germany's shoe billionaire, established Wortmann KG in 1967, in the city of Detmold in North Rhine-Westphalia.
Considered the European market leader in women's fashionable shoes, its brands include Tamaris, Marco Tozzi, Caprice, Jana and s.Oliver.
Nephew Jens Beining developed "Agenda 2020" to prepare the company for future challenges, with special focus on online retail.
Heir apparent Beining, who assumed operational management control in 2016, owns 10% of the company.
The company, operating under the umbrella of Wortmann Schuh-Holding KG, has about 1,100 direct employees and an overall workforce of 30,000.
forbes_facts: Wortmann runs a real estate business on the side.

name: Phornthep Phornprapha
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Hurun Global (2014-2021)
forbes_bio: Phornthep Phornprapha runs privately held Siam Motors Group, producer of Nissan cars and trucks in Thailand.
The family's other interests include auto parts, logistics, construction equipment and hotels.
Siam Motors has funded an automotive engineering and development center at Thammasat University's campus in Pattaya.
forbes_facts: Phornthep has a board seat at Bangkok Bank, controlled by the Sophonpanich family.
The company is building a 30-story tower in downtown Bangkok, which is expected to open in 2022.

name: Stephane Courbit
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Wikidata (2023)
forbes_bio: Stephane Courbit is the chairman of Banijay Group, an independent production and distribution firm.
Courbit owns a 45% stake in the publicly traded company, whose 170,000+ hours of programming including Survivor and Peaky Blinders.
He started his career at production studio Coyote and then in 1994 formed his own production company with TV host Arthur
Four years later, billionaire John de Mol's Endemol merged that outfit to form Endemol France, which Courbit ran as CEO.
After leaving in 2007, Courbit set up privately held LOV Group, through which he operates Airelles, a collection of 7 boutique hotels including 3 palaces.
Through LOV, he also owns 740 acres of vineyards and olive trees plus Macaron maker Laduree.

name: Chen Yung-tai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Yung-tai got his start selling office clocks in 1965. He later expanded into office equipment, furniture and electronics.
Today his listed Aurora Corp., chaired by wife Yuan Hui-Hua since 2018, sells electronics in over 1,500 locations in Taiwan and mainland China.
Aurora also owns real estate, including a 38-story tower, in Shanghai's Lujiazui financial district.
Chen studied economics in college. That department is now part of National Taipei University.
forbes_facts: Chen was born into a well-off family but worked as a small trader and street merchant after his father died in his youth.
Chen founded the Aurora Museum in Shanghai, known for its Buddhist sculptures and jade.

name: Mohammad Abunayyan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Mohammad Abunayyan is the founder and chairman of ACWA Power, a Saudi power generation and water desalination firm.
He founded the company in 2004 and took it public on the Saudi stock exchange in 2021; he now owns 3.5% of the shares.
Abunayyan also chairs Vision Invest, a Saudi holding company that owns stakes in several publicly traded and privately held companies.
He also owns 8% of Abdullah Abunayyan Trading Company, a Saudi holding company that owns 50% of Vision Invest.
Vision Invest and Abunayyan Holding own shares in several Saudi publicly traded companies in wastewater treatment, logistics and flour milling.

name: Artur Grynbaum
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Artur Grynbaum is the brother-in-law of Miguel Krigsner, who founded Brazil's second-largest cosmetics company Grupo Boticario.
Grynbaum joined as a financial assistant and worked his way up to president of the group by 2008. He owns about 20% of the company.
Grupo Boticario operates in more than 50 countries; Krigsner individually owns approximately 80% of the business.
Today, Krigsner and Grynbaum serve as president and vice president, respectively, of the Grupo Boticario advisory board.
In 1990 Krigsner created the Boticario Group Foundation dedicated to environmental protection, which receives about 1% of Grupo Boticario's net income annually.

name: Anand Burman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Anand Burman is the fifth-generation scion of the storied Burman clan.
After more than a decade, he stepped down as  chairman of the family company Dabur, India's fourth-largest consumer goods company, in 2019.
His wealth is mostly derived from his stake in the Delhi-headquartered company, known for its hair oil, fruit juices and health supplements.
He also has stakes in Kolkata-based dry-cell battery maker Eveready and New Delhi-based financial services group Religare.
His cousin, Mohit, is now chairman of Dabur, while his son, Aditya, is a director.
forbes_facts: Burman has invested in his personal capacity in home healthcare services, cancer diagnostics and life sciences.
Falguni Nayar, the billionaire founder of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, sits on Dabur's board.

name: Jacob Burda
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2020); Hurun Global (2021)
forbes_bio: Jacob Burda, son of publishing magnate Hubert Burda and doctor and actress Maria Furtwaengler, owns 25% of Burda Media Group.
Its portfolio consists of some 600 media products in 24 countries, including Focus and Bunte and the German editions of Elle and Harper's Bazaar.
He is a member of the Burda Media's board of directors, as is his sister Elisabeth Furtwaengler.
While father Hubert has spoken of Jacob eventually becoming CEO of the publishing group, no concrete succession plans have been announced.
Jacob has invested in a variety of startups, particularly in the United States, and helped finance the Berlin Palace's reconstruction.
forbes_facts: In 2019, Jacob, with a PhD in early German romanticism from Oxford University, taught a course in German literature and philosophy at UCLA.
His sister Elisabeth, also a billionaire, performs as a singer-songwriter under the stage name Lisa Fou.

name: Will Wei Cheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021-2022); Forbes annual (2020-2021)
forbes_bio: Cheng Wei is CEO of ride-hailing firm Didi Global, which listed its shares on the New York Stock Exchange in June 2021.
Days after Didi went public, the Chinese government announced a cybersecurity review and banned Didi's app from the app store.
Before founding Didi Dache, Cheng worked at Alibaba and was vice president for Alibaba's online payment service Alipay.
Didi was formed in 2015 when Cheng's company Didi Dache merged with Alibaba-backed competitor Kuaidi Dache. Didi acquired Uber China in 2016.

name: Subhash Chandra
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2019); Forbes annual (2000-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2019); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Subhash Chandra chairs media giant Essel Group, which also has interests in amusement parks, packaging, infrastructure and lotteries.
Broadcaster Zee Entertainment Enterprises, run by Chandra's sons Punit and Amit, has 76 channels reaching 1.3 billion viewers in 173 countries.
Chandra has entered the cruise business under the brand Jalesh, which means "God of the water."
Weighed down by debt in his infrastructure business, Chandra said in November 2018, that he was looking to sell part of his stake in flagship Zee.
In January 2019, shares of his companies took a hit on an allegation that Essel was linked to a company under investigation for fraud. Essel denied the allegation.
forbes_facts: Chandra and his three brothers marked Essel's 90th anniversary in May 2017 by pledging $777 million to their DSC Foundation.
Chandra is a member of parliament and meditates daily.
